title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence Workflows, and Exceptions
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Purpose

This document centralizes Redwood Inference's security and compliance controls for: RBAC & authentication, audit logging and retention, data residency and retention, secure SDLC controls, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk & exceptions handling. It is intended for engineers, SRE, product security reviewers, and audit owners.

Scope

- Applies to hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments (control plane and data plane).
- Covers cloud resources (AWS, GCP), on-prem packaging, and third-party vendor integrations.

Owner and contact

- Document owner: Security (Ava Martinez)
- Primary contacts: security-oncall (PagerDuty), compliance@redwood.com
- Evidence owner: Compliance Engineering (Ethan Walker)

1) RBAC and Authentication

Overview

- Principle: Least privilege by default; role-based access mapped to job functions. Use group-based assignments in Okta and short-lived service credentials for machine accounts.
- Supported identities: human (SSO via Okta + MFA), service principals (OIDC for CI/CD), and on-prem service accounts (mutual TLS).

Standard Roles (examples)

| Role | Description | Typical Owners | Can perform |
|---|---|---|---|
| security-admin | Full security config and audit access | Security team | Manage policies, view audit artifacts |
| platform-admin | Infra and platform operations | Eng Platform | Deploy infra, configure autoscaling |
| svc-inference | Inference service principals | Eng Serving Runtime | Read/write model KV caches, route traffic |
| readonly-audit | Read-only access to logs and dashboards | SRE, Auditors | Query logs, create reports |

Policies and Controls

- Access provisioning: All role assignments request via Access Jira (ACCESS-REQ ticket), approved by role owner and manager.
- Review cadence: Quarterly access reviews (90 days) automated via Identity Governance; deviations flagged to managers.
- Service credential rotation: All long-lived keys are forbidden. Use short-lived OIDC tokens or Vault-issued leases (max TTL 24 hours).
- Separation of duties: No single user may be both platform-admin and security-admin in production. Exceptions documented in risk register.
- Break-glass process: Emergency access requests go through the security-oncall flow; approved via PagerDuty incident and audited (see Emergency Access Runbook).

2) Audit Logging and Monitoring

Goals

- Ensure tamper-evident, queryable audit trail for security-relevant actions: RBAC changes, infra changes, deployment rollouts, key material access, and data exports.
- Retain sufficient detail for incident investigations and compliance audits.

What we log

- IAM events (Okta: user/group changes, SSO failures)
- Platform changes (terraform apply, cluster scaling, configuration updates)
- API access and admin actions against the Redwood Control Plane (model uploads, model-pinning, routing policy changes)
- Secrets and KMS usage metadata (key IDs, caller identity — not plaintext secrets)
- Data exports and data residency transfers

Logging pipeline & retention

- Ingestion: Logs routed to the centralized telemetry pipeline (CloudWatch/Logging -> Kinesis/Log Router -> Splunk/Datadog as primary SIEM).
- Integrity: Audit logs are signed and checksummed at ingestion; daily integrity reports are produced and archived to encrypted evidence buckets.
- Retention defaults:
  - Security audit logs: 3 years (encrypted, stored in evidence S3/GCS with SSE-KMS).
  - Operational logs (metrics/traces): 90 days hot, 2 years cold (aggregated).
  - Compliance evidence artifacts (audit bundles): 7 years.
- SLO for log availability: 99.9% of audit events indexed in SIEM within 5 minutes of ingestion.
- Alerting: Critical security events (privilege grants, failed privileged logins >5 in 10m, unexpected KMS key usage) trigger PagerDuty to security-oncall.

Common queries and examples

- Search authorizations for a user in Splunk: splunk query: "index=audit user=alice action=grant* OR action=role*"
- GCP example to fetch admin IAM changes: gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName:"SetIamPolicy"' --freshness=1d

3) Data Residency and Retention

Residency policy

- Customers may choose region for data residency when onboarding (US, EU, APAC). For dedicated/private deployments, data is stored in customer-selected region and access is limited to matching region control plane where possible.
- Cross-region transfers are prohibited unless authorized in the contract and documented with data flow map and approved compensating controls.

Retention policy (data types)

| Data Type | Default Retention | Rationale |
|---|---:|---|
| PII (user-provided prompts/metadata) | 90 days | Minimize exposure; customers can request shorter thresholds |
| Model artifacts (non-sensitive) | Indefinite (versioned) | For reproducibility and rollbacks |
| Audit logs | 3 years | Regulatory and investigation needs |
| Billing records | 7 years | Financial and legal requirements |
| Compliance evidence buckets | 7 years | Auditability |

Data deletion and customer requests

- Data deletion requests follow the data-subject-request (DSR) workflow: submit ticket to privacy@redwood.com -> request triaged -> owner executes deletion using owner-specific runbook -> provide signed attestation.
- Deletion verification: run Hash-based proofs and provide a deletion report (commands and hashes) stored in the evidence bucket.

Encryption & key management

- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers; mutual TLS for service-to-service in private deployments.
- At-rest: SSE-KMS for cloud object storage. Key lifecycle managed by Security (rotate primary keys every 2 years, rotate data keys per-project every 90 days). HSM available for enterprise customers on request.

4) Secure SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle)

Mandates

- All production code must pass the following gates before merge to main and deploy to prod:
  1. Code review by at least one peer + one security reviewer for high-risk changes.
  2. Automated unit/integration tests with >= 80% coverage on critical modules.
  3. Static analysis: Semgrep and built-in linters; high-severity findings block merge.
  4. Dependency scanning: Snyk or equivalent; critical CVEs must be fixed or mitigated.
  5. Secret scanning: Git pre-commit hooks and CI-level scans; any detected secret triggers rotation and a review.
  6. CI gating: All checks must pass; artifacts are signed and stored with build metadata and SBOM.

Release controls and runtime hardening

- Canary rollouts for new inference runtime and model-serving changes with automated rollback on error-rate > 1% or latency regression > 40%.
- Runtime sandboxing: model execution constrained by resource quotas and seccomp profiles in hosted environments.

Developer training and evidence

- Mandatory secure-coding training for engineers annually.
- Each release links to the PR with security checklist items as compliance evidence.

5) Incident Response — Security-Specific Procedures

Overview and priority model

- Incident classification: P0 (data exfiltration, active compromise of production keys), P1 (privilege escalation, large-scale data exposure), P2 (suspected but contained), P3 (informational).
- PagerDuty routing: P0/P1 -> security-oncall + incident commander; P2 -> security-oncall; P3 -> ticket to security triage.

Initial triage and containment (runbook excerpt)

1. Triage: Acknowledge PagerDuty, capture initial indicators (IPs, user IDs, timestamps).
2. Containment: Rotate affected keys via KMS/Vault, isolate compromised instances (ASG/instance drain or Kubernetes cordon+evict).
3. Evidence collection:
   - Snapshot affected VMs/containers (preserve disk and memory where needed).
   - Export relevant audit logs and SIEM search results to an evidence bundle (S3/GCS path).
   - Record chain-of-custody: who accessed evidence, why, and actions taken.
4. Communication: Notify legal and customer success for data-affecting incidents per the notification policy.
5. Root cause & remediation: Conduct RCA within 72 hours for P0/P1; produce remediation plan and verify patching.

Evidence bundle contents (minimum)

- Timestamped export of audit logs (OKTA, infra, control-plane)
- Config snapshots (terraform state, cluster manifests)
- Affected application logs and traces
- Exported memory/dump (if applicable) and hash values
- Chain-of-custody document (signed)

6) Compliance Evidence Workflows

Quarterly and ad-hoc evidence generation

- Compliance owners will run the Evidence Collector job (automated) which assembles:
  - Monthly access review reports
  - Signed KMS rotation logs
  - SBOMs for deployed artifacts
  - SDLC gate checklists per release
  - Incident evidence bundles (when applicable)
- Artifact storage: Evidence artifacts are stored in encrypted, immutable buckets (S3 Object Lock enabled for required retention periods). Access to evidence requires approval and is logged.

Auditor access process

1. Auditor requests sent to compliance@redwood.com.
2. Compliance triages scope, provisions temporary auditor accounts or generates signed-presigned URLs with least privilege and time-limited access.
3. All auditor sessions recorded and logged.

7) Risk & Exceptions

Exception process

- Use the Risk Exceptions form (Risk-EX-YYYYMMDD) to request temporary deviations from policy. Required fields: owner, impacted systems, compensating controls, expiration date (max 90 days), and approver signatures (security director + affected area manager).
- Approval tiers:
  - Low risk (non-prod config): security lead approval.
  - Medium risk (prod but mitigated): security manager + platform manager.
  - High risk (prod with customer data): security director + legal + exec sponsor.

Mitigations and re-evaluation

- All exceptions must include compensating controls (e.g., additional logging, network ACLs, increased monitoring). Exceptions are tracked in the Risk Register and re-evaluated at 30/60/90 days. Unrenewed exceptions are automatically revoked.

Audit readiness and periodic reviews

- Annual internal audit and third-party SOC2/ISO assessments on a 12-month cadence.
- Evidence readiness checklist maintained by Compliance Engineering; monthly dry-run where sample auditors request artifacts.

Appendices

A. Useful commands and queries

- Rotate a KMS key (example): aws kms schedule-key-deletion --key-id <key-id> --pending-window-in-days 7
- Export recent terraform state changes: terraform state pull | jq . > state-YYYYMMDD.json
- SIEM search example (Splunk): index=audit (action=grant OR action=role_change) | stats count by user, action

B. Ownership matrix (summary)

- Security: Policy owner, incident response, KMS management
- Compliance Engineering: Evidence automation, evidence buckets, auditor coordination
- Eng Platform: RBAC enforcement, infra IAM controls, key distribution integration
- Eng Serving Runtime: Runtime hardening, model pinning controls
